sources.title: Amazon announces ‘Melania, The Series’ after airing first lady’s documentary - The Washington Post
passages: The new program, titled “Melania, The Series,” will begin airing Nov.
The production follows Amazon’s decision to acquire and market a documentary earlier this year about the first lady.
That film, “Melania,” sparked criticism that Amazon was seeking to curry favor with the Trump administration, and several Democrats opened an investigation .
Amazon on Friday announced a two-part docu-series focused on first lady Melania Trump’s return to Washington in early 2025, saying the program will provide “unprecedented insight” into her life.
Amazon founder Jeff Bezos, who owns The Washington Post, has denied that the film was an effort to win influence, distanced himself from its production and said it was a business decision.
Amazon reportedly spent $40 million to acquire the documentary and an additional $35 million to promote it.
The new show will include events recorded after the January 2025 inauguration, according to a news release from Amazon.
An Amazon spokesperson said Friday that the original licensing deal for the documentary also covered the new series.

extraction.body: State and city officials in Pennsylvania are condemning as antisemitic a planned bike protest in Philadelphia urging boycotts of a half-dozen Jewish-owned restaurants. The event called for noon Sunday is being organized, according to local station WPVI-TV, by several groups, including Philly Bike On Your Left. Officials and critics say the businesses are being targeted because they are owned by Jews, and are lambasting ride organizers. Gov. Josh Shapiro (D) said in a statement Thursday that the bike ride “masquerading as a protest to advance the cause of justice, is nothing more than blatant antisemitism designed to intimidate and drive Jewish businesses out of our communities.” Attorney General Dave Sunday called the event “unconscionable” in a statement . He noted that the protest will happen a day before the anniversary of Kristallnacht, a massive, deadly state-approved 1938 pogrom in Nazi Germany and Austria against synagogues and Jewish businesses. Ride organizers referred WPVI-TV to a statement by a group calling for a boycott of restaurants owned by the group CookNSolo, which focuses on Israeli cuisine. The statement said that one of the restaurant group’s owners has partnered with the Israeli Ministry of Tourism and that several restaurants hosted free events for Israeli soldiers, among other reasons. A call for comment to CookNSolo wasn’t immediately returned Friday. The ride organizers’ statement also said “Zionists have mounted a coordinated campaign to discredit and villainize the organizers and detract from their anti-genocide message.” Critics’ references to Kristallnacht are “cynical,” the statement added. Catch up quickly with a rundown of the 7 most important and interesting stories. In the blue tide overtaking the country this week, Alabama voters elected the first openly gay sheriff as well as the state’s first openly transgender legislator. Democrat Brett Jones, in Madison County, defeated a two-term Republican incumbent to take over the law enforcement role. Jones is a former Navy SEAL who wrote a 2014 book about his experience of being gay in the military called “Pride: The Story of the First Openly Gay Navy SEAL.” Jones, a police officer at the University of Alabama at Huntsville, campaigned on transparency, jail reform and discontinuing the county’s contract with Flock, the controversial license plate reader system that has sparked widespread concern about overreaching government surveillance . Its supporters, including Gov. Ron DeSantis (R) and Florida Realtors, described it as much-needed relief for millions of homeowners. Amendment 3 , as it is widely known, would extend the state’s homestead exemption from the current $50,000 a year per eligible home to $150,000 beginning in 2027. That number would rise to $250,000 in 2028. New residents have to live in Florida for five years before qualifying for expanded exemptions. “You vote for it, you’ll pay less. End of story,” DeSantis said in one September news conference. But the amendment faced broad opposition from mayors and city managers, police and fire chiefs, and advocacy groups who warned the policy would deprive local governments of billions of dollars — and lead to painful cuts in key services. Despite those pleas, on Tuesday the measure cleared the 60 percent of support required to pass, receiving about 62 percent of votes. DeSantis said Wednesday he plans to call a special session before his term ends for lawmakers to work out the details for implementation. In addition, Gov.-elect Byron Donalds has said he hopes to eliminate homestead property taxes in the state entirely. NAIROBI — Paul Nthenge Mackenzie, a cult leader in Kenya who was found guilty last month of the murder of 191 people, all but one of them children, was sentenced Friday to 200 years in prison. Judge Diana Kavedza, reading the sentence in a courtroom in Mombasa, Kenya, said Mackenzie would serve the prison time for murder by starvation and murder by direct homicide, 100 years for each. The televangelist, now 53, was arrested in April 2023 after at least 400 people, mostly members of his Good News International Church, were found buried in shallow graves in the Shakahola Forest in Kenya’s coastal region. Some of the dead have never been identified. During court proceedings, relatives and friends accused Mackenzie of indoctrinating his congregation with doomsday sermons. He discouraged modern medicine, including vaccinations, and government initiatives such obtaining identification cards and participating in the census. Fox Corp. on Friday announced it had completed its $22 billion deal to take over Roku, one of the leading smart TV companies. “Beginning today, our top priority for the combined company is to continue to relentlessly serve audiences and partners, while reinforcing the openness and choice that is the essence of the Roku platform,” Lachlan Murdoch, executive chair and CEO of Fox Corp., wrote in a news release. The deal, announced in June , will plunge Fox deeper into the Hollywood streaming wars, years after it sold off its own film and television studio, then called 21st Century Fox, to Disney for $71 billion in 2019. It will also give Fox an advantage in free, ad-supported streaming at a time when large streamers are embracing advertising to complement their subscription plans. Fox already owned Tubi and now will also own the Roku Channel — two of the leaders in free-to-stream media. However, Fox promised the government that it would continue carrying content from its competitors on Roku’s platform for at least three years, and said it won’t discriminate against rival media companies using the platform. Amazon on Friday announced a two-part docu-series focused on first lady Melania Trump’s return to Washington in early 2025, saying the program will provide “unprecedented insight” into her life. The new program, titled “Melania, The Series,” will begin airing Nov. 20 on Prime Video. The production follows Amazon’s decision to acquire and market a documentary earlier this year about the first lady. That film, “Melania,” sparked criticism that Amazon was seeking to curry favor with the Trump administration, and several Democrats opened an investigation . Amazon founder Jeff Bezos, who owns The Washington Post, has denied that the film was an effort to win influence, distanced himself from its production and said it was a business decision. The new show will include events recorded after the January 2025 inauguration, according to a news release from Amazon. Brett Ratner, who directed the documentary, also directed the episodes of the new show. An Amazon spokesperson said Friday that the original licensing deal for the documentary also covered the new series. Amazon reportedly spent $40 million to acquire the documentary and an additional $35 million to promote it. Celebrities typically apologize for their wrongdoings with a statement via Notes app — but Martha Stewart went further this week after she dressed up as a homeless person for Halloween, sparking intense backlash. It didn’t end there: TMZ soon posted footage of Stewart at a Florida corporate event, saying that she threw together the costume after she appeared on the “Today” show, and during a cooking segment, co-host Craig Melvin spilled chocolate on her sweater — one that she was supposed to wear later to a Halloween party. Finally, it all culminated on Friday with Stewart completing the ultimate celebrity mea culpa: Going on live morning television to apologize in person. During a brief and slightly awkward interview, Stewart sat down with Melvin and explained that she did not blame him for the chocolate-spilling incident. Stewart emphasized she did not mean to make light of any social issues, and recognizes the costume was a mistake: “I was stupid. What else can I say? I’m so sorry, and I hope that my followers and my fans and the rest of America forgives me for doing something that was not meant in any way to be a bad thing.” Melvin and Stewart agreed that she would like to move on, and that the “Today” show will see her again next week to talk about cooking for Thanksgiving.

extraction.body: State and city officials in Pennsylvania are condemning as antisemitic a planned bike protest in Philadelphia urging boycotts of a half-dozen Jewish-owned restaurants. The event called for noon Sunday is being organized, according to local station WPVI-TV, by several groups, including Philly Bike On Your Left. Officials and critics say the businesses are being targeted because they are owned by Jews, and are lambasting ride organizers. Gov. Josh Shapiro (D) said in a statement Thursday that the bike ride “masquerading as a protest to advance the cause of justice, is nothing more than blatant antisemitism designed to intimidate and drive Jewish businesses out of our communities.” Attorney General Dave Sunday called the event “unconscionable” in a statement . He noted that the protest will happen a day before the anniversary of Kristallnacht, a massive, deadly state-approved 1938 pogrom in Nazi Germany and Austria against synagogues and Jewish businesses. Ride organizers referred WPVI-TV to a statement by a group calling for a boycott of restaurants owned by the group CookNSolo, which focuses on Israeli cuisine. The statement said that one of the restaurant group’s owners has partnered with the Israeli Ministry of Tourism and that several restaurants hosted free events for Israeli soldiers, among other reasons. A call for comment to CookNSolo wasn’t immediately returned Friday. The ride organizers’ statement also said “Zionists have mounted a coordinated campaign to discredit and villainize the organizers and detract from their anti-genocide message.” Critics’ references to Kristallnacht are “cynical,” the statement added. In the blue tide overtaking the country this week, Alabama voters elected the first openly gay sheriff as well as the state’s first openly transgender legislator. Democrat Brett Jones, in Madison County, defeated a two-term Republican incumbent to take over the law enforcement role. Jones is a former Navy SEAL who wrote a 2014 book about his experience of being gay in the military called “Pride: The Story of the First Openly Gay Navy SEAL.” Jones, a police officer at the University of Alabama at Huntsville, campaigned on transparency, jail reform and discontinuing the county’s contract with Flock, the controversial license plate reader system that has sparked widespread concern about overreaching government surveillance . Its supporters, including Gov. Ron DeSantis (R) and Florida Realtors, described it as much-needed relief for millions of homeowners. Amendment 3 , as it is widely known, would extend the state’s homestead exemption from the current $50,000 a year per eligible home to $150,000 beginning in 2027. That number would rise to $250,000 in 2028. New residents have to live in Florida for five years before qualifying for expanded exemptions. “You vote for it, you’ll pay less. End of story,” DeSantis said in one September news conference. But the amendment faced broad opposition from mayors and city managers, police and fire chiefs, and advocacy groups who warned the policy would deprive local governments of billions of dollars — and lead to painful cuts in key services. Despite those pleas, on Tuesday the measure cleared the 60 percent of support required to pass, receiving about 62 percent of votes. DeSantis said Wednesday he plans to call a special session before his term ends for lawmakers to work out the details for implementation. In addition, Gov.-elect Byron Donalds has said he hopes to eliminate homestead property taxes in the state entirely. NAIROBI — Paul Nthenge Mackenzie, a cult leader in Kenya who was found guilty last month of the murder of 191 people, all but one of them children, was sentenced Friday to 200 years in prison. Judge Diana Kavedza, reading the sentence in a courtroom in Mombasa, Kenya, said Mackenzie would serve the prison time for murder by starvation and murder by direct homicide, 100 years for each. The televangelist, now 53, was arrested in April 2023 after at least 400 people, mostly members of his Good News International Church, were found buried in shallow graves in the Shakahola Forest in Kenya’s coastal region. Some of the dead have never been identified. During court proceedings, relatives and friends accused Mackenzie of indoctrinating his congregation with doomsday sermons. He discouraged modern medicine, including vaccinations, and government initiatives such obtaining identification cards and participating in the census. The deal, announced in June , will plunge Fox deeper into the Hollywood streaming wars, years after it sold off its own film and television studio, then called 21st Century Fox, to Disney for $71 billion in 2019. It will also give Fox an advantage in free, ad-supported streaming at a time when large streamers are embracing advertising to complement their subscription plans. Celebrities typically apologize for their wrongdoings with a statement via Notes app — but Martha Stewart went further this week after she dressed up as a homeless person for Halloween, sparking intense backlash. It didn’t end there: TMZ soon posted footage of Stewart at a Florida corporate event, saying that she threw together the costume after she appeared on the “Today” show, and during a cooking segment, co-host Craig Melvin spilled chocolate on her sweater — one that she was supposed to wear later to a Halloween party. Finally, it all culminated on Friday with Stewart completing the ultimate celebrity mea culpa: Going on live morning television to apologize in person. During a brief and slightly awkward interview, Stewart sat down with Melvin and explained that she did not blame him for the chocolate-spilling incident. Stewart emphasized she did not mean to make light of any social issues, and recognizes the costume was a mistake: “I was stupid. What else can I say? I’m so sorry, and I hope that my followers and my fans and the rest of America forgives me for doing something that was not meant in any way to be a bad thing.” Melvin and Stewart agreed that she would like to move on, and that the “Today” show will see her again next week to talk about cooking for Thanksgiving.
passages: State and city officials in Pennsylvania are condemning as antisemitic a planned bike protest in Philadelphia urging boycotts of a half-dozen Jewish-owned restaurants.
The event called for noon Sunday is being organized, according to local station WPVI-TV, by several groups, including Philly Bike On Your Left.
Officials and critics say the businesses are being targeted because they are owned by Jews, and are lambasting ride organizers.

Gov. Josh Shapiro (D) said in a statement Thursday that the bike ride “masquerading as a protest to advance the cause of justice, is nothing more than blatant antisemitism designed to intimidate and drive Jewish businesses out of our communities.”

Attorney General Dave Sunday called the event “unconscionable” in a statement . He noted that the protest will happen a day before the anniversary of Kristallnacht, a massive, deadly state-approved 1938 pogrom in Nazi Germany and Austria against synagogues and Jewish businesses.

Ride organizers referred WPVI-TV to a statement by a group calling for a boycott of restaurants owned by the group CookNSolo, which focuses on Israeli cuisine. The statement said that one of the restaurant group’s owners has partnered with the Israeli Ministry of Tourism and that several restaurants hosted free events for Israeli soldiers, among other reasons.
A call for comment to CookNSolo wasn’t immediately returned Friday.

The ride organizers’ statement also said “Zionists have mounted a coordinated campaign to discredit and villainize the organizers and detract from their anti-genocide message.” Critics’ references to Kristallnacht are “cynical,” the statement added.

In the blue tide overtaking the country this week, Alabama voters elected the first openly gay sheriff as well as the state’s first openly transgender legislator.

Democrat Brett Jones, in Madison County, defeated a two-term Republican incumbent to take over the law enforcement role. Jones is a former Navy SEAL who wrote a 2014 book about his experience of being gay in the military called “Pride: The Story of the First Openly Gay Navy SEAL.”

Jones, a police officer at the University of Alabama at Huntsville, campaigned on transparency, jail reform and discontinuing the county’s contract with Flock, the controversial license plate reader system that has sparked widespread concern about overreaching government surveillance .

Its supporters, including Gov. Ron DeSantis (R) and Florida Realtors, described it as much-needed relief for millions of homeowners. Amendment 3 , as it is widely known, would extend the state’s homestead exemption from the current $50,000 a year per eligible home to $150,000 beginning in 2027. That number would rise to $250,000 in 2028. New residents have to live in Florida for five years before qualifying for expanded exemptions.
“You vote for it, you’ll pay less. End of story,” DeSantis said in one September news conference.

But the amendment faced broad opposition from mayors and city managers, police and fire chiefs, and advocacy groups who warned the policy would deprive local governments of billions of dollars — and lead to painful cuts in key services.
Despite those pleas, on Tuesday the measure cleared the 60 percent of support required to pass, receiving about 62 percent of votes.

DeSantis said Wednesday he plans to call a special session before his term ends for lawmakers to work out the details for implementation. In addition, Gov.-elect Byron Donalds has said he hopes to eliminate homestead property taxes in the state entirely.
NAIROBI — Paul Nthenge Mackenzie, a cult leader in Kenya who was found guilty last month of the murder of 191 people, all but one of them children, was sentenced Friday to 200 years in prison.
Judge Diana Kavedza, reading the sentence in a courtroom in Mombasa, Kenya, said Mackenzie would serve the prison time for murder by starvation and murder by direct homicide, 100 years for each.

The televangelist, now 53, was arrested in April 2023 after at least 400 people, mostly members of his Good News International Church, were found buried in shallow graves in the Shakahola Forest in Kenya’s coastal region. Some of the dead have never been identified.

During court proceedings, relatives and friends accused Mackenzie of indoctrinating his congregation with doomsday sermons. He discouraged modern medicine, including vaccinations, and government initiatives such obtaining identification cards and participating in the census.

“Beginning today, our top priority for the combined company is to continue to relentlessly serve audiences and partners, while reinforcing the openness and choice that is the essence of the Roku platform,” Lachlan Murdoch, executive chair and CEO of Fox Corp., wrote in a news release.

The deal, announced in June , will plunge Fox deeper into the Hollywood streaming wars, years after it sold off its own film and television studio, then called 21st Century Fox, to Disney for $71 billion in 2019.

However, Fox promised the government that it would continue carrying content from its competitors on Roku’s platform for at least three years, and said it won’t discriminate against rival media companies using the platform.

The Wall Street Journal previously reported some details of the funding.

Private valuations like these often hint at where public markets are heading. A trimmed target suggests investors now want proof, not just promises. Also, OpenAI pushed back its plans to go public, and a listing is now widely expected sometime in 2027.

This cash buys it time. Third, it’s a reality check for the whole AI trade. If you hold tech stocks, AI-themed funds, or even crypto tokens riding the AI narrative, sentiment around OpenAI ripples straight into your portfolio.

coreStoryFacts.text: (Bloomberg) -- OpenAI has closed on new funding of roughly $11 billion, the initial part of a round that values the company at $1.25 trillion, according to people familiar with the matter.The funding was wired to the company as of Friday, said the people, who spoke on condition of anonymity as the information is not public.

The remainder of the round, which could increase to as much as $20 billion in total, is expected to be completed in the coming weeks, one person said.The AI developer has been in talks for more than a month to raise a large funding round after delaying its plans for an initial public offering.
The Wall Street Journal previously reported some details of the funding.
The reduced funding goals represent a stark shift for a fundraising juggernaut that helped usher in the current AI boom.
OpenAI has reportedly raised $11 billion so far in a new funding round that values the AI lab at $1.25 trillion.

The news comes only hours after Bloomberg also reported that potential buyers of shares in the IPO of OpenAI’s chief competitor, Anthropic, are eyeing a substantially lower valuation than Anthropic had targeted.
Bloomberg writes that some potential buyers believe Anthropic’s valuation could be as low as $1.1 trillion, compared with the $2 trillion that investors were said to be expecting roughly a month ago.
The current figures fall well short of that target.
Bloomberg reported on the new funding on Friday, citing sources familiar with the matter.
The round is expected to close in the coming weeks and could total about $20 billion, a source told Bloomberg.
TechCrunch has reached out to OpenAI for comment and will update this story if it responds.
OpenAI previously intimated that it would go public this year but subsequently delayed its plans.
There are expectations that the company will IPO next year at some point.
It’s believed that OpenAI could raise up to $9 billion in additional funding as part of the round.
The deal is expected to value the company at $1.25 billion.
That potentially puts it on track to surpass Anthropic PBC’s market capitalization.
The list of possible participants includes Microsoft Corp., which contributed to at least four of OpenAI’s previous rounds.
That included its most recent $122 billion raise in March, which also drew the participation of Nvidia Corp., Amazon.com Inc. and about two dozen others.
Anthropic hopes to achieve a valuation of $1.5 trillion in its upcoming initial public offering.
However, several of its investors reportedly don’t consider that to be a realistic goal.
According to the Wall Street Journal , one shareholder reportedly suggested that the company pursue a valuation closer to $1 trillion.
Anthropic’s IPO filing revealed that its quarterly revenue jumped 1,127% on a year-over-year basis in the third quarter.
The company’s growth was driven by its enterprise business, which saw sales more than double.
The latest addition to OpenAI’s enterprise portfolio debuted on Thursday.

passages: TSMC rises on report of potential push into advanced memory for Nvidia
ADRs of TSMC surged 7.7% in early trading Friday as investors weighed the prospect of the foundry giant deepening its role in the critical AI hardware supply chain.

The Taiwanese manufacturer recently began formulating plans to produce vertically stacked 3D DRAM at the behest of its primary customer, NVIDIA (NASDAQ:NVDA), according to two people with direct knowledge of the matter cited by The Information.
Yahoo Finance is not a broker-dealer or investment adviser and does not offer securities or cryptocurrencies for sale or facilitate trading.
The company's exploration is being spearheaded by Hsu Kuo-chin, a vice president directing TSMC's advanced packaging operations who previously ran Micron's regional footprint.

His oversight underscores how intimately memory architecture has become linked with advanced packaging, the specialized process required to tether memory and processing units into cohesive computing systems.
TSMC is examining whether to construct dedicated fabrication facilities or acquire and retool an existing site to support the specialized production, the report indicated.

That latter path mirrors a maneuver by Micron Technology Inc (NASDAQ:MU), which in March agreed to purchase a Taiwan-based facility from Powerchip Semiconductor Manufacturing Corp. for $1.8 billion to retrofit for high-end memory.
A persistent bottleneck in memory availability has driven hardware costs sharply higher, prompting key buyers such as Nvidia and Apple (NASDAQ:AAPL) to actively seek alternative procurement channels.
Apple, for its part, implemented price increases across its hardware portfolio earlier this year after absorbing substantial increases in memory procurement expenses.
Entering the memory arena would nonetheless expose TSMC to a notoriously volatile segment long dominated by Samsung Electronics (KS:005930), SK hynix Inc (NASDAQ:SKHY), and Micron.

Memory markets are historically prone to severe boom-and-bust supply imbalances, and while TSMC holds proprietary patents around vertical DRAM, translating lab designs into defect-free volume manufacturing poses formidable execution hurdles.

The strategic shift also introduces delicate competitive dynamics, particularly following TSMC's 2024 pact to manufacture base logic dies for SK Hynix's next-generation high-bandwidth memory products.

That was still enough to move Micron and SK Hynix, which says a lot about how jittery the AI supply chain has become.

TSMC built its reputation as a logic foundry.
It manufactures processors designed by other companies, rather than selling its own branded chips.
The research also raises a second path: partnerships with existing memory specialists.
That route would let TSMC expand its footprint without building an entire memory operation from scratch.
For AI chip buyers, including Nvidia, the stakes look different.

The research suggests that if TSMC succeeds, its 3D DRAM output could help stabilize pricing.
The research describes semiconductor companies increasingly chasing vertically integrated setups to cope with supply chain disruptions.

There is also a strategic dimension worth watching: the research indicates a TSMC memory push could reshape alliances across the memory space and encourage investment in new technologies built for AI workloads.
Several signals will matter in the months ahead.

coreStoryFacts.text: The Taiwanese company recently began drafting plans to produce a particular type of advanced memory chips, known as 3D DRAM, at the request of Nvidia Corp. , its biggest customer, The Information reported, citing two people familiar with the plans.

TSMC rises on report of potential push into advanced memory for Nvidia
ADRs of TSMC surged 7.7% in early trading Friday as investors weighed the prospect of the foundry giant deepening its role in the critical AI hardware supply chain.

The Taiwanese manufacturer recently began formulating plans to produce vertically stacked 3D DRAM at the behest of its primary customer, NVIDIA (NASDAQ:NVDA), according to two people with direct knowledge of the matter cited by The Information.
Yahoo Finance is not a broker-dealer or investment adviser and does not offer securities or cryptocurrencies for sale or facilitate trading.
The company's exploration is being spearheaded by Hsu Kuo-chin, a vice president directing TSMC's advanced packaging operations who previously ran Micron's regional footprint.

His oversight underscores how intimately memory architecture has become linked with advanced packaging, the specialized process required to tether memory and processing units into cohesive computing systems.
TSMC is examining whether to construct dedicated fabrication facilities or acquire and retool an existing site to support the specialized production, the report indicated.

That latter path mirrors a maneuver by Micron Technology Inc (NASDAQ:MU), which in March agreed to purchase a Taiwan-based facility from Powerchip Semiconductor Manufacturing Corp. for $1.8 billion to retrofit for high-end memory.
A persistent bottleneck in memory availability has driven hardware costs sharply higher, prompting key buyers such as Nvidia and Apple (NASDAQ:AAPL) to actively seek alternative procurement channels.
Apple, for its part, implemented price increases across its hardware portfolio earlier this year after absorbing substantial increases in memory procurement expenses.
Entering the memory arena would nonetheless expose TSMC to a notoriously volatile segment long dominated by Samsung Electronics (KS:005930), SK hynix Inc (NASDAQ:SKHY), and Micron.

Memory markets are historically prone to severe boom-and-bust supply imbalances, and while TSMC holds proprietary patents around vertical DRAM, translating lab designs into defect-free volume manufacturing poses formidable execution hurdles.

The strategic shift also introduces delicate competitive dynamics, particularly following TSMC's 2024 pact to manufacture base logic dies for SK Hynix's next-generation high-bandwidth memory products.
According to a report from The Information, Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Company is considering a push into advanced memory chips, with internal plans focused on 3D DRAM .
The report ties the effort to demand from Nvidia , TSMC’s largest client.
The key word throughout is “considering.” TSMC is described as formulating plans, not breaking ground on memory fabs.
No timeline, investment figure, or production target appears in the reporting.
That was still enough to move Micron and SK Hynix, which says a lot about how jittery the AI supply chain has become.
TSMC, the company that builds the brains of the AI boom, is reportedly thinking about building its memory too.
TSMC built its reputation as a logic foundry.
It manufactures processors designed by other companies, rather than selling its own branded chips.
The research also raises a second path: partnerships with existing memory specialists.

Yahoo Finance is not a broker-dealer or investment adviser and does not offer securities or cryptocurrencies for sale or facilitate trading.
The company's exploration is being spearheaded by Hsu Kuo-chin, a vice president directing TSMC's advanced packaging operations who previously ran Micron's regional footprint.

His oversight underscores how intimately memory architecture has become linked with advanced packaging, the specialized process required to tether memory and processing units into cohesive computing systems.
TSMC is examining whether to construct dedicated fabrication facilities or acquire and retool an existing site to support the specialized production, the report indicated.

That latter path mirrors a maneuver by Micron Technology Inc (NASDAQ:MU), which in March agreed to purchase a Taiwan-based facility from Powerchip Semiconductor Manufacturing Corp. for $1.8 billion to retrofit for high-end memory.
A persistent bottleneck in memory availability has driven hardware costs sharply higher, prompting key buyers such as Nvidia and Apple (NASDAQ:AAPL) to actively seek alternative procurement channels.
Apple, for its part, implemented price increases across its hardware portfolio earlier this year after absorbing substantial increases in memory procurement expenses.
Entering the memory arena would nonetheless expose TSMC to a notoriously volatile segment long dominated by Samsung Electronics (KS:005930), SK hynix Inc (NASDAQ:SKHY), and Micron.

Memory markets are historically prone to severe boom-and-bust supply imbalances, and while TSMC holds proprietary patents around vertical DRAM, translating lab designs into defect-free volume manufacturing poses formidable execution hurdles.

The strategic shift also introduces delicate competitive dynamics, particularly following TSMC's 2024 pact to manufacture base logic dies for SK Hynix's next-generation high-bandwidth memory products.

passages: Three US lawmakers have asked Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang to brief Congress over reported Chinese espionage concerns involving Megaspeed.

The request follows reports that Huang had interacted with an executive of Megaspeed International who was reportedly under US government surveillance over allegations of supplying information to China.
The lawmakers have sought a closed-door congressional briefing on November 18 to examine Nvidia’s dealings with the executive and its safeguards for sensitive technology.
Representatives Brian Mast, John Moolenaar and Rick Crawford signed the letter requesting Huang’s appearance.
The three Republican lawmakers lead congressional panels responsible for foreign affairs, China-related issues and intelligence matters.
The congressional request comes amid continuing disagreements over American semiconductor exports to China.
Nvidia has faced scrutiny from lawmakers concerned that advanced artificial intelligence processors could strengthen China’s military and technological capabilities.
The allegations have raised concerns about whether individuals associated with Beijing could obtain sensitive American technology or information through commercial relationships.
Under the original proposal, sales of Nvidia’s H200 processors could face congressional intervention, while its Blackwell generation and subsequent advanced chips would be subject to restrictions.
Lawmakers would have been able to block specific transactions through a joint resolution.
A revised version has progressed in the Senate without the provision allowing Congress to block individual sales through joint resolutions.
The measure is being considered for possible inclusion in an annual defence spending package.
The controversy also comes as Democrats prepare to assume control of congressional committees following the midterm elections.
The incoming leadership has indicated plans for closer scrutiny of major technology companies.

The lawmakers wrote, “ Recent reports raise significant national security concerns regarding the PRC’s access to sensitive US technology and information .” They said Congress needed to determine whether American national security had been compromised.
Nvidia has rejected suggestions that its interactions with customers necessarily indicate security concerns.

A company spokesperson said Huang engages with thousands of customers annually and expressed confidence that US authorities would notify Nvidia if they considered any individual a threat to American industry.
In January, he accused the company and its chief executive of seeking to sell millions of advanced chips to Chinese businesses and challenged Huang to a televised debate.
Earlier this year, Mast also helped develop the proposed AI Overwatch Act, which sought to give Congress greater authority over exports of advanced AI processors.
The proposal included an approval mechanism resembling congressional oversight of certain arms sales.

The lawmakers have sought a closed-door congressional briefing on November 18 to examine Nvidia’s dealings with the executive and its safeguards for sensitive technology. The scrutiny follows a report by The New York Times concerning Huang Le, an executive at Megaspeed International, who was reportedly under surveillance by US authorities over suspected links to Chinese intelligence activities. The allegations have raised concerns about whether individuals associated with Beijing could obtain sensitive American technology or information through commercial relationships. Representatives Brian Mast, John Moolenaar and Rick Crawford signed the letter requesting Huang’s appearance. The three Republican lawmakers lead congressional panels responsible for foreign affairs, China-related issues and intelligence matters. They want Nvidia to explain the nature of its interactions with the Megaspeed executive and the security measures governing such relationships. The lawmakers wrote, “ Recent reports raise significant national security concerns regarding the PRC’s access to sensitive US technology and information .” They said Congress needed to determine whether American national security had been compromised. Nvidia has rejected suggestions that its interactions with customers necessarily indicate security concerns. A company spokesperson said Huang engages with thousands of customers annually and expressed confidence that US authorities would notify Nvidia if they considered any individual a threat to American industry. The lawmakers, however, have requested further clarification about the company’s dealings with Megaspeed International. Their proposed joint briefing would take place behind closed doors and focus on Nvidia’s internal security procedures and measures intended to prevent unauthorised access to sensitive technology. The congressional request comes amid continuing disagreements over American semiconductor exports to China. Nvidia has faced scrutiny from lawmakers concerned that advanced artificial intelligence processors could strengthen China’s military and technological capabilities. Mast has previously criticised Nvidia’s position on export restrictions. In January, he accused the company and its chief executive of seeking to sell millions of advanced chips to Chinese businesses and challenged Huang to a televised debate. Earlier this year, Mast also helped develop the proposed AI Overwatch Act, which sought to give Congress greater authority over exports of advanced AI processors. The proposal included an approval mechanism resembling congressional oversight of certain arms sales. Under the original proposal, sales of Nvidia’s H200 processors could face congressional intervention, while its Blackwell generation and subsequent advanced chips would be subject to restrictions. Lawmakers would have been able to block specific transactions through a joint resolution. A revised version has progressed in the Senate without the provision allowing Congress to block individual sales through joint resolutions. The measure is being considered for possible inclusion in an annual defence spending package. The controversy also comes as Democrats prepare to assume control of congressional committees following the midterm elections. The incoming leadership has indicated plans for closer scrutiny of major technology companies. Nvidia, meanwhile, continues to oppose overly restrictive export policies as Washington debates the national security implications of supplying advanced computing technology to China. The scrutiny follows a report by The New York Times concerning Huang Le, an executive at Megaspeed International, who was reportedly under surveillance by US authorities over suspected links to Chinese intelligence activities. The congressional request comes amid continuing disagreements over American semiconductor exports to China. Nvidia has faced scrutiny from lawmakers concerned that advanced artificial intelligence processors could strengthen China’s military and technological capabilities.

Earlier this year, Mast also helped develop the proposed AI Overwatch Act, which sought to give Congress greater authority over exports of advanced AI processors. The proposal included an approval mechanism resembling congressional oversight of certain arms sales.

The measure is being considered for possible inclusion in an annual defence spending package.

The controversy also comes as Democrats prepare to assume control of congressional committees following the midterm elections. The incoming leadership has indicated plans for closer scrutiny of major technology companies.
Nvidia, meanwhile, continues to oppose overly restrictive export policies as Washington debates the national security implications of supplying advanced computing technology to China.

coreStoryFacts.text: Top Republican lawmakers have asked Jensen Huang to appear before Congress to answer questions after it was reported that US intelligence officials believe Nvidia’s chief executive has been targeted by a Chinese spying operation.
“Meetings with customers are part of a CEO’s job.
Jensen talks with thousands of customer executives every year,” the company said.
Lawmakers want answers about Jensen Huang’s ties to an alleged Chinese intelligence asset.
“The issue of PRC infiltration and access to cutting-edge US technology is core to the investigative work of our three committees this Congress.
It is vital that Congress determines the extent to which US national security has been placed at risk,” the lawmakers added.
The US has previously scrutinized Megaspeed, founded in 2023 as a spin-off from a Chinese gaming company, for potential chip smuggling, although no charges followed.
The New York Times said Huang had not received a “defensive briefing,” which the intelligence community usually, but not always, provides potential espionage targets to warn them about the activity.

Nvidia said it was confident that the US government would have let the company know if it thought a person was a threat to US industry and that it often receives updates from Washington about people of concern.

Nvidia launched its own unannounced on-site inspections at Megaspeed in Singapore when it became aware of the US concerns, but the internal probe found no evidence of its chips being diverted into China, said people familiar with the matter.
Congress has summoned Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang to directly explain his relationship with a woman suspected of being a Chinese spy.

According to Axios on the 5th (local time), Representative Brian Mast, Republican Chairman of the House Foreign Affairs Committee, Representative John Moolenaar, Chairman of the House Select Committee on the Chinese Communist Party, and Representative Rick Crawford, member of the Intelligence Committee, sent a letter to Jensen Huang that day, requesting his attendance at a joint, closed-door briefing by the three committees.
Alice Huang herself reportedly flaunted her ties by posting photos with Jensen Huang on social media, which she allegedly used to raise investment funds.

The Chinese government previously dismissed allegations of Chinese espionage targeting Nvidia as "groundless speculation." (Photo: Capture of a NetThunder LinkedIn post, Yonhap News) ※ Please note: This article was translated by AI and may contain errors.
In the letter, they asked Huang to explain Nvidia's security systems designed to protect the company from foreign adversaries, as well as his interactions with Alice Huang.
Nvidia has not released a statement regarding the House's summons.
Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang has been called before the US Congress to answer questions about his ties to a woman facing allegations of spying for China.
Alice Huang was photographed sitting next to Jensen Huang at a bar in Taiwan in June 2024, drinking with executives from other AI companies, and was again seen accompanying him in May last year.
The chairs cited recent media reports raising national security concerns about the possible leakage of sensitive US technology to China.

"Chinese penetration and access to advanced American technology is a core investigative matter for all three committees this session," they wrote, adding that the extent of any national security exposure must be thoroughly assessed.
The Wall Street Journal reported that officials from at least three countries have expressed concern about the possibility that Alice Huang leaked information about Nvidia chips.

A revised version has progressed in the Senate without the provision allowing Congress to block individual sales through joint resolutions.

The incoming leadership has indicated plans for closer scrutiny of major technology companies.

relevantPassages.text: Three US lawmakers have asked Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang to brief Congress over reported Chinese espionage concerns involving Megaspeed.

The request follows reports that Huang had interacted with an executive of Megaspeed International who was reportedly under US government surveillance over allegations of supplying information to China.
The lawmakers have sought a closed-door congressional briefing on November 18 to examine Nvidia’s dealings with the executive and its safeguards for sensitive technology.
Representatives Brian Mast, John Moolenaar and Rick Crawford signed the letter requesting Huang’s appearance.
The three Republican lawmakers lead congressional panels responsible for foreign affairs, China-related issues and intelligence matters.
The congressional request comes amid continuing disagreements over American semiconductor exports to China.
Nvidia has faced scrutiny from lawmakers concerned that advanced artificial intelligence processors could strengthen China’s military and technological capabilities.
The allegations have raised concerns about whether individuals associated with Beijing could obtain sensitive American technology or information through commercial relationships.
Under the original proposal, sales of Nvidia’s H200 processors could face congressional intervention, while its Blackwell generation and subsequent advanced chips would be subject to restrictions.
Lawmakers would have been able to block specific transactions through a joint resolution.
A revised version has progressed in the Senate without the provision allowing Congress to block individual sales through joint resolutions.
The measure is being considered for possible inclusion in an annual defence spending package.
The controversy also comes as Democrats prepare to assume control of congressional committees following the midterm elections.
The incoming leadership has indicated plans for closer scrutiny of major technology companies.

The lawmakers wrote, “ Recent reports raise significant national security concerns regarding the PRC’s access to sensitive US technology and information .” They said Congress needed to determine whether American national security had been compromised.
Nvidia has rejected suggestions that its interactions with customers necessarily indicate security concerns.

A company spokesperson said Huang engages with thousands of customers annually and expressed confidence that US authorities would notify Nvidia if they considered any individual a threat to American industry.
In January, he accused the company and its chief executive of seeking to sell millions of advanced chips to Chinese businesses and challenged Huang to a televised debate.
Earlier this year, Mast also helped develop the proposed AI Overwatch Act, which sought to give Congress greater authority over exports of advanced AI processors.
The proposal included an approval mechanism resembling congressional oversight of certain arms sales.

The report ties the effort to demand from Nvidia , TSMC’s largest client.
The key word throughout is “considering.” TSMC is described as formulating plans, not breaking ground on memory fabs.
No timeline, investment figure, or production target appears in the reporting.
That was still enough to move Micron and SK Hynix, which says a lot about how jittery the AI supply chain has become.
TSMC, the company that builds the brains of the AI boom, is reportedly thinking about building its memory too.
TSMC built its reputation as a logic foundry.
It manufactures processors designed by other companies, rather than selling its own branded chips.
The research also raises a second path: partnerships with existing memory specialists.
That route would let TSMC expand its footprint without building an entire memory operation from scratch.
For AI chip buyers, including Nvidia, the stakes look different.
More memory supply could relieve a constraint that has been capping how fast AI hardware ships.
The research suggests that if TSMC succeeds, its 3D DRAM output could help stabilize pricing.
The research describes semiconductor companies increasingly chasing vertically integrated setups to cope with supply chain disruptions.

There is also a strategic dimension worth watching: the research indicates a TSMC memory push could reshape alliances across the memory space and encourage investment in new technologies built for AI workloads.
Several signals will matter in the months ahead.
Watch for any official confirmation from TSMC, any disclosed partnership with an established memory maker, and any comment from Nvidia on its memory sourcing.

sources.title: Meta introduces Spaces, a new way to collaborate with your Muse agent
passages: Meta recently launched its Muse agents — a new generation of cuddly agentic helpers.
Now, the company has launched Spaces, a new way to communicate and collaborate with them.

As far as I can tell, Spaces are basically breakout conversations that revolve around a particular topic — although Meta refers to them as “custom experiences.” They live in the sidebar of the interface where you interact with your Muse agent.
Clicking on the Space brings up the conversation, where Muse works toward a particular goal on your behalf.

For instance, if you wanted to plan a vacation, you could open a new Space focused on that particular project, and whenever you want to work on it with Muse, you would click to open that particular tab.
Other examples Meta gives are a holiday gift tracker, a wedding planner, or a space for DIY projects.
On Friday, Mark Zuckerberg, Meta’s founder and CEO, posted about the new feature on X: “Playing around with spaces in Muse lately — tell Muse what you need and it builds it.
I’ve made a BBQ game, an event tracker, and a home control dashboard.
The company is obviously busy building out the user experience around the agents.
Spaces is actually the second new Muse feature that Meta has debuted over the last week.
On Thursday, the company also announced Muse Voice , which allows users to video chat with their agent and give it commands verbally.
Spaces can also be easily integrated with third-party apps and information, Meta says.
Muse agents — and the cuddly avatars that enclose them — have been greeted with a relatively warm reception over the past few months.
During its earnings call in October, Zuckerberg said that its agents had 10 million users in the U.S. and Canada — less than two months after the agents debuted.

Firefly Aerospace said AST will pay it more than $1.3 billion in cash and stock over three years for 36 engines, a license to manufacture them and engineering support. Firefly will deliver 27 Miranda and nine Vira engines for the first three rockets. AST says Blacklift is a three-stage vehicle with two reusable lower stages that can carry up to five BlueBirds per mission and will complement its existing launch partners.
Microsoft is winding down a 2023 deal to rent AI cloud capacity from Oracle, Bloomberg reports

Microsoft is winding down a 2023 arrangement to rent AI computing capacity from Oracle after declining to renew the contract, Bloomberg reported, citing people familiar with the matter. The capacity, which supported Microsoft's AI-powered Bing search engine, used older-generation Nvidia chips that no longer fit Microsoft's specifications. Microsoft declined to comment. Oracle said demand for its AI infrastructure remains strong and that GPU capacity up for renewal in its first quarter was renewed or resold at a 20% premium for long-term contracts.
OpenAI launches GPT-6 Cyber, which found 81 high-severity Firefox flaws

OpenAI released GPT-6 Cyber on November 5, a GPT-6 Astra model trained for authorized vulnerability research. It found 81 previously unknown Firefox vulnerabilities Mozilla rated high severity, and Mozilla has shipped fixes for many. In Linux kernel research, it reproduced 1,724 vulnerabilities and developed working exploits for 948. Access starts with approved Daybreak Red customers through the API and Codex.

extraction.body: Meta has a new way to talk to its AI without putting on a pair of glasses.At the end of Wednesday's Meta Connect keynote, CEO Mark Zuckerberg unveiled Muse Charm, a small, always-on handheld device built around Muse, Meta's AI assistant. The Tamagotchi-like gadget is designed for people who don't wear Meta's smart glasses, and Zuckerberg called it the fastest way to talk to Muse without wearing them. SEE ALSO: Meet the Meta Ray-Ban Gen 3, starting at $249 The reveal was set up earlier in the keynote. During a live demo, Zuckerberg used Meta's glasses to talk with his customized Muse assistant, which he'd named Agrippa, about a handheld device he was working on. That device turned out to be Muse Charm.Muse sat at the center of this year's keynote. Meta describes it as a personal agent that can set goals, share ideas, and run tasks in the background, and users can customize its personality and voice. Zuckerberg also suggested Meta could eventually collect a small fee on transactions the assistant helps complete.Muse Charm will ship by the holidays in December, according to Zuckerberg. Meta did not announce a price and said more details will come later.The device enters a category with a rocky track record. Standalone AI gadgets like Humane's Ai Pin and the Rabbit R1 drew harsh reviews after launching in 2024, and Humane discontinued the AI Pin the following year. Muse Charm's main selling point is that it runs on the same assistant as Meta's glasses.

coreStoryFacts.text: Meta recently launched its Muse agents — a new generation of cuddly agentic helpers.
Now, the company has launched Spaces, a new way to communicate and collaborate with them.

As far as I can tell, Spaces are basically breakout conversations that revolve around a particular topic — although Meta refers to them as “custom experiences.” They live in the sidebar of the interface where you interact with your Muse agent.
Clicking on the Space brings up the conversation, where Muse works toward a particular goal on your behalf.

For instance, if you wanted to plan a vacation, you could open a new Space focused on that particular project, and whenever you want to work on it with Muse, you would click to open that particular tab.
Other examples Meta gives are a holiday gift tracker, a wedding planner, or a space for DIY projects.
On Friday, Mark Zuckerberg, Meta’s founder and CEO, posted about the new feature on X: “Playing around with spaces in Muse lately — tell Muse what you need and it builds it.
I’ve made a BBQ game, an event tracker, and a home control dashboard.
The company is obviously busy building out the user experience around the agents.
Spaces is actually the second new Muse feature that Meta has debuted over the last week.
On Thursday, the company also announced Muse Voice , which allows users to video chat with their agent and give it commands verbally.
Spaces can also be easily integrated with third-party apps and information, Meta says.
Muse agents — and the cuddly avatars that enclose them — have been greeted with a relatively warm reception over the past few months.
During its earnings call in October, Zuckerberg said that its agents had 10 million users in the U.S. and Canada — less than two months after the agents debuted.

TechCrunch names OpenAI's dots and SpaceXAI's Grokbot as competing agent products.

AST SpaceMobile plans to develop its own rocket, Blacklift, to launch its BlueBird satellites. Firefly Aerospace said AST will pay it more than $1.3 billion in cash and stock over three years for 36 engines, a license to manufacture them and engineering support. Firefly will deliver 27 Miranda and nine Vira engines for the first three rockets. AST says Blacklift is a three-stage vehicle with two reusable lower stages that can carry up to five BlueBirds per mission and will complement its existing launch partners.

Microsoft is winding down a 2023 arrangement to rent AI computing capacity from Oracle after declining to renew the contract, Bloomberg reported, citing people familiar with the matter. The Tamagotchi-like gadget is designed for people who don't wear Meta's smart glasses, and Zuckerberg called it the fastest way to talk to Muse without wearing them. SEE ALSO: Meet the Meta Ray-Ban Gen 3, starting at $249 The reveal was set up earlier in the keynote. During a live demo, Zuckerberg used Meta's glasses to talk with his customized Muse assistant, which he'd named Agrippa, about a handheld device he was working on. That device turned out to be Muse Charm.Muse sat at the center of this year's keynote. Meta describes it as a personal agent that can set goals, share ideas, and run tasks in the background, and users can customize its personality and voice. Zuckerberg also suggested Meta could eventually collect a small fee on transactions the assistant helps complete.Muse Charm will ship by the holidays in December, according to Zuckerberg. Meta did not announce a price and said more details will come later.The device enters a category with a rocky track record. Standalone AI gadgets like Humane's Ai Pin and the Rabbit R1 drew harsh reviews after launching in 2024, and Humane discontinued the AI Pin the following year. Muse Charm's main selling point is that it runs on the same assistant as Meta's glasses.

sources.title: TSMC rises on report of potential push into advanced memory for Nvidia - Yahoo Finance
passages: TSMC rises on report of potential push into advanced memory for Nvidia
ADRs of TSMC surged 7.7% in early trading Friday as investors weighed the prospect of the foundry giant deepening its role in the critical AI hardware supply chain.

The Taiwanese manufacturer recently began formulating plans to produce vertically stacked 3D DRAM at the behest of its primary customer, NVIDIA (NASDAQ:NVDA), according to two people with direct knowledge of the matter cited by The Information.
Yahoo Finance is not a broker-dealer or investment adviser and does not offer securities or cryptocurrencies for sale or facilitate trading.
The company's exploration is being spearheaded by Hsu Kuo-chin, a vice president directing TSMC's advanced packaging operations who previously ran Micron's regional footprint.

His oversight underscores how intimately memory architecture has become linked with advanced packaging, the specialized process required to tether memory and processing units into cohesive computing systems.
TSMC is examining whether to construct dedicated fabrication facilities or acquire and retool an existing site to support the specialized production, the report indicated.

That latter path mirrors a maneuver by Micron Technology Inc (NASDAQ:MU), which in March agreed to purchase a Taiwan-based facility from Powerchip Semiconductor Manufacturing Corp. for $1.8 billion to retrofit for high-end memory.
A persistent bottleneck in memory availability has driven hardware costs sharply higher, prompting key buyers such as Nvidia and Apple (NASDAQ:AAPL) to actively seek alternative procurement channels.
Apple, for its part, implemented price increases across its hardware portfolio earlier this year after absorbing substantial increases in memory procurement expenses.
Entering the memory arena would nonetheless expose TSMC to a notoriously volatile segment long dominated by Samsung Electronics (KS:005930), SK hynix Inc (NASDAQ:SKHY), and Micron.

Memory markets are historically prone to severe boom-and-bust supply imbalances, and while TSMC holds proprietary patents around vertical DRAM, translating lab designs into defect-free volume manufacturing poses formidable execution hurdles.

The strategic shift also introduces delicate competitive dynamics, particularly following TSMC's 2024 pact to manufacture base logic dies for SK Hynix's next-generation high-bandwidth memory products.

relevantPassages.text: TSMC rises on report of potential push into advanced memory for Nvidia
ADRs of TSMC surged 7.7% in early trading Friday as investors weighed the prospect of the foundry giant deepening its role in the critical AI hardware supply chain.

The Taiwanese manufacturer recently began formulating plans to produce vertically stacked 3D DRAM at the behest of its primary customer, NVIDIA (NASDAQ:NVDA), according to two people with direct knowledge of the matter cited by The Information.
Yahoo Finance is not a broker-dealer or investment adviser and does not offer securities or cryptocurrencies for sale or facilitate trading.
The company's exploration is being spearheaded by Hsu Kuo-chin, a vice president directing TSMC's advanced packaging operations who previously ran Micron's regional footprint.

His oversight underscores how intimately memory architecture has become linked with advanced packaging, the specialized process required to tether memory and processing units into cohesive computing systems.
TSMC is examining whether to construct dedicated fabrication facilities or acquire and retool an existing site to support the specialized production, the report indicated.

That latter path mirrors a maneuver by Micron Technology Inc (NASDAQ:MU), which in March agreed to purchase a Taiwan-based facility from Powerchip Semiconductor Manufacturing Corp. for $1.8 billion to retrofit for high-end memory.
A persistent bottleneck in memory availability has driven hardware costs sharply higher, prompting key buyers such as Nvidia and Apple (NASDAQ:AAPL) to actively seek alternative procurement channels.
Apple, for its part, implemented price increases across its hardware portfolio earlier this year after absorbing substantial increases in memory procurement expenses.
Entering the memory arena would nonetheless expose TSMC to a notoriously volatile segment long dominated by Samsung Electronics (KS:005930), SK hynix Inc (NASDAQ:SKHY), and Micron.

Memory markets are historically prone to severe boom-and-bust supply imbalances, and while TSMC holds proprietary patents around vertical DRAM, translating lab designs into defect-free volume manufacturing poses formidable execution hurdles.

The strategic shift also introduces delicate competitive dynamics, particularly following TSMC's 2024 pact to manufacture base logic dies for SK Hynix's next-generation high-bandwidth memory products.

extraction.body: Apple says well over 100,000 apps are now built for the iPhone Duo, a count it reached about two weeks after the foldable went on sale. The figure came from Apple itself, and CNET carried the statement from Susan Prescott, Apple’s vice president of Worldwide Developer Relations. She said, “Today there are well over 100,000 apps built for iPhone Duo already live on the App Store, and thousands of optimized apps are being added to the store each day.” That is the whole quantitative claim. Apple gave no exact count beyond the round number, and this analysis treats it that way. The milestone arrives while shoppers are still asking whether the device is worth waiting for. Our earlier report on iPhone Duo delivery quotes slipping to Jan. 22 covered the supply side. This piece covers the software side: what 100,000 optimized apps does and does not prove, which apps Apple named, and what the number means for the hardware race in foldables. Apple reportedly released the iPhone Duo on October 23, 2026, and the milestone statement followed on November 6. That is a 14-day window in which developers had to get hardware or simulators, rebuild against a new SDK, test two display configurations and push updates through App Review. Apple says more than 100,000 apps cleared that path, with thousands more arriving daily. Several outlets ran the same core fact on the same day. GSMArena, CNET, MacRumors, AppleInsider, 9to5Mac, MacStories and The Apple Post all reported the figure, and each tied it to Apple’s own wording. When that many independent newsrooms repeat one number on one afternoon, it usually means Apple distributed it directly. That matters for how you read it. The count is a company claim, delivered by the company, with no third-party audit attached. Still, the claim is specific enough to test over time. Apple says the apps are live, not announced, and that they target the iPhone Duo itself. Anyone with a device or an App Store account can spot-check named titles against that statement. The sections below do exactly that with the apps Apple listed. Separating confirmed facts from open questions is the first job in any milestone story. The table below lists what the reporting supports and what remains unstated. It is built only from Apple’s statement and the coverage that repeated it. Two gaps stand out. First, Apple gave no sales figure, so nobody can compute apps per owner or judge whether developers are chasing a large installed base. Second, the company gave no breakdown by category, so the 100,000 could skew toward small utilities or toward heavy productivity titles. Readers should hold both gaps open until more data appears. Reports say the counted apps were built with the iOS 27.1 SDK or later. That detail narrows the claim in a useful way. An app that merely runs on the iPhone Duo through compatibility scaling does not qualify. The number refers to apps that developers recompiled and adjusted for the new hardware, which is a higher bar than simple installability. MacRumors, whose report carried the headline “Here’s What’s Still Missing,” said it confirmed that the figure refers to apps built with that SDK. The headline itself signals that a gap remains between the 100,000 and the full catalog people expect on a flagship phone. MacRumors did not turn that gap into a number in the text we reviewed, and we do not guess one here. For engineers, the SDK gate has a practical effect. Reports on Apple’s developer guidance say standard SwiftUI and UIKit components adapt to both displays, so teams that already use those frameworks face a lighter lift than teams with custom layout engines. Apps with hard-coded screen assumptions need real work. That split likely explains why Apple can claim six figures within two weeks while still leaving visible holes. The iPhone Duo has two screens, and the reporting describes optimization as support for both. Apple’s wording, as relayed by outlets, says optimized apps use the full width of the inner and outer displays and place vertical controls in the status bar. That is a layout rule, not a cosmetic touch. It changes where buttons sit and how content flows when the device opens or closes. CNET described a 4:3 main screen and said Apple’s milestone shows developers adapting to it. A squarer canvas than a standard phone changes the design math. Lists can become two columns, editors can show a document beside a toolbar, and video apps can pick between letterboxing and reflowing their interface. Apps that simply stretch a phone layout look wrong on that shape, which is why the optimization label carries weight. The outer screen is the other half of the test. An app that looks good open but breaks when closed will draw complaints within days. Apple’s phrase about the full width of both displays tells us the counted apps handle both states. It does not tell us how well each app handles the transition mid-task, such as a video call that survives a fold or a draft that stays in place. Those behaviors will surface in app reviews over the coming weeks. Apple named a long list of optimized apps, and the grouping tells a story. Productivity and communication titles dominate, with a strong showing from Microsoft. Media, shopping, sports and AI assistants fill out the rest. The table sorts the named apps by category using only Apple’s list. That is 28 named titles out of a claimed 100,000-plus, so the list is a sample and not a census. Even so, the sample leans toward work and reading. Seven office tools and four notes apps suggest the early target audience uses a larger inner screen for documents, email and meetings. Streaming and sports apps point to a second use case, watching content on the squarer panel. Prescott’s remarks appear in several outlets, and they carry two messages. The first is the count. The second is tone. As 9to5Mac reported, she said, “It’s been wonderful to see how quickly developers have embraced iPhone Duo, and we’re grateful for their creativity and innovation.” That sentence frames the milestone as a developer success story, which suits Apple’s relationship with the people who build its platform. A second statement, reported by The Verge , looks forward. Prescott said, “The enthusiasm has been incredible, and we’re excited to see the pace of updates continue to accelerate as more and more apps optimize for iPhone Duo.” The phrase about accelerating updates sets an expectation that the daily additions will keep growing. Apple has now put that expectation on the record, which makes later slowdowns easier to spot. Both quotes come from a vice president whose job is developer relations, not sales. That role shapes the message. Developer relations teams want more apps, so they publish adoption numbers that encourage hesitant studios to join. A buyer reading the same statement should remember the audience. The point is to recruit developers, and it does that well. New form factors have always struggled with software. Early Android foldables, including Samsung’s first Galaxy Fold in 2019, shipped into an ecosystem where many apps did not know how to resize across a fold. Google later pushed large-screen guidance and launched its own Pixel Fold in 2023, and tablet-style layouts slowly became a normal expectation for Android developers. The lesson from that period is that hardware arrives first and software follows, sometimes by years. Apple faces a similar problem but holds a different set of tools. It controls the SDK, the review process and the storefront, and it can tell developers exactly which build version qualifies. The company also has a record of coaxing app support for new device classes, from the original iPad in 2010 to later screen-size changes on the iPhone. The 100,000 figure in two weeks fits that pattern of coordinated platform pushes. Two things set the iPhone Duo apart from earlier foldable launches. Apple appears to have asked developers to target the device before and during release, and it is counting only apps built with the newer SDK. A stricter definition makes the headline number harder to inflate. By contrast, older foldable ecosystems often cited compatible apps, a looser measure that included anything that merely launched. The strongest argument for Apple is consistency. A single SDK, a single store and one hardware family let the company roll out layout rules everywhere at once. The strongest argument against is scale. Android has years of large-screen experience across many makers, and its developers have spent that time learning to handle odd shapes. Apple compresses that learning curve into weeks, but compression is not the same as depth. For developers, the milestone redraws the cost-benefit math. A studio that skipped Android foldables might still adapt for the Duo because Apple customers tend to spend heavily on apps and because the company will likely feature early adopters. Teams with sibling iPad apps hold an edge, since iPad layouts already solve many of the same problems. Smaller teams without that code base need to budget for a few weeks of rework. For the wider hardware industry, the story sits inside a growing foldable segment. Mordor Intelligence’s forecast, which we covered when it projected foldable phones reaching $138.4B by 2032 , assumed that software support would improve as big platform owners joined. Apple’s entry and this early app push give that assumption some evidence, though one milestone does not validate a multi-year forecast. Component suppliers for hinges, flexible displays and thin glass stand to benefit only if consumer demand matches developer enthusiasm. Finally, watch your crash and review data after release. Fold transitions create edge cases that simulators miss, such as state loss during a posture change. Early reviews on the App Store will tell you quickly whether the update works. A fast follow-up patch costs little and protects ratings during the launch window when Apple’s featuring teams are paying attention. Several questions have no public answer today. Apple has not provided an exact app total, a split by category or a count of how many of the 100,000 are new apps versus updates to existing ones. It has not shared iPhone Duo pricing in the milestone statement, nor sales, specifications beyond what outlets described, or a roadmap for further SDK changes. Anyone presenting those details as settled is going beyond the record. The quality of optimization is also unmeasured. A count of apps built for the Duo tells us they target the device. It does not tell us how many use both displays well, how many ship with bugs or how many just meet the minimum. Independent testers will fill that gap over time. Until they do, treat the 100,000 as a measure of effort and not of polish. The Duo is not the only Apple device drawing developer attention this year. Rumors about the next Pro iPhone, including the under-display Face ID reports for the iPhone 18 Pro , show Apple working on several screen changes at once. Each change asks developers to revisit layouts, and a smooth Duo rollout makes the next one easier to sell. The company also gains a testing ground. Lessons from the Duo’s two-display behavior can inform future products, and developers who now understand posture-aware layouts will carry that skill forward. In that sense, the 100,000 figure is less about one phone and more about training an entire developer base for what comes next. Hardware cycles run for years, and software habits stick. How many apps are optimized for iPhone Duo? Apple says well over 100,000 apps are built for the device and live on the App Store. It gave no exact total, and outlets reporting the news repeated that wording. When did the iPhone Duo launch? Reports give October 23, 2026 as the launch date. Apple’s milestone statement is dated November 6, 2026, two weeks later. Which apps are already optimized? Apple named Microsoft Word, Excel, PowerPoint and Outlook, Zoom, Etsy, Halide Mark III, Spotify, CBS, Tubi, BBC iPlayer (UK), Apple Music Classical, NBA, NHL, Yahoo Fantasy Sports, Sportsnet (Canada), Facebook Messenger, Google Chat, ChatGPT, Grok Bot, Microsoft Copilot, SAP Concur, monday.com, Extra, Goodnotes, PDF Expert, Documents and iA Writer. What does optimized mean in practice? According to reports, optimized apps support the full width of the inner and outer displays and place vertical controls in the status bar. CNET described the main screen as 4:3. Does the milestone show how well the iPhone Duo is selling? No. Apple did not disclose sales, price or detailed specifications in the statement, so the app count cannot stand in for demand.

extraction.body: Apple today announced that more than 100,000 apps have been optimized for the iPhone Duo, released two weeks ago. We confirmed that this figure refers to apps built with the iOS 27.1 SDK or later , meaning these apps fill the full width of the iPhone Duo's inner and outer displays and have vertical controls in the status bar. A statement from Susan Prescott, Apple's Vice President of Worldwide Developer Relations: It's been wonderful to see how quickly developers have embraced iPhone Duo, and we're grateful for their creativity and innovation. Today there are well over 100,000 apps built for iPhone Duo already live on the App Store, and thousands of optimized apps are being added to the store each day. In the last month alone, thousands of developers have joined us for workshops in 19 cities around the world to experience iPhone Duo firsthand and bring updated apps to their users. The enthusiasm has been incredible, and we're excited to see the pace of updates continue to accelerate as more and more apps optimize for iPhone Duo. Apple said thousands of apps optimized for the iPhone Duo are being added to the App Store each day, with recent examples including Microsoft's Excel, OneNote, PowerPoint, and Word apps , along with the Etsy, Goodnotes, Halide Mark III, NBA, NHL, and Zoom apps. Other apps optimized for the device include Amazon Prime Video, Fantastical, Flighty, Instagram, MLB, Netflix, SmartGym, WhatsApp, YouTube, and more. There are too many to list. Apps optimized for the iPhone Duo have a "Made for iPhone Duo" badge in their App Store listings on the device, making them easy to identify. iOS 27.2 added Apple Pencil (USB-C) support to the iPhone Duo , enabling users to draw in apps like Procreate Pocket, take notes in Apple Notes, Fineliner, and TypeDraw, and mark up documents in apps like Preview on the device. On the other hand, with millions of apps available in the App Store, there are unsurprisingly many apps that are still not optimized for the iPhone Duo, with the following examples listed in alphabetical order: AMC Theaters, Amazon Fire TV, Apple Store, Best Buy, Bluesky, Delta, DoorDash, Duolingo, Fandango, FedEx, Goodreads, Google Docs, Google Home, Google Sheets, Google Slides, GrubHub, JetBlue, Libby, Microsoft Authenticator, Microsoft Teams, MTA, Nike, PayPal, PictureThis, Ring, Southwest, Spectrum TV, Starbucks, Steam, Uber Eats, UPS, USPS, Venmo, Verizon, Wells Fargo, Whole Foods, and YouTube Music. Apple said developers can easily optimize their apps for the iPhone Duo. Apps that use standard SwiftUI and UIKit components adapt automatically to each display, with controls moved to the status bar and multi-column support on the inner display. New APIs let developers optimize their apps for the device's various layouts and poses. Apple has hosted more than 50 in-person iPhone Duo app workshops in 19 cities worldwide, and there are online resources like the Apple Developer Forums . In the meantime, apps built with the iOS 27 SDK resize to fill most of the inner display on the iPhone Duo, but they avoid the status bar on the right edge. It is clearly a mixed bag, with some apps optimized and some not. More apps are being updated by the day, though, so the situation is improving rapidly. Apple's iPhone Duo is in customers' hands, and our dedicated how-to series explains the new features worth trying first. Spec bump to the M6 chip for the low-end 14-inch model, plus new high-end PROLED XDR models with touchscreen displays. 8.5-inch OLED display, A20 Pro chip, IP67 water and dust resistance, and a thinner and lighter design. Apple's smart home hub with 7-inch square display, A18 chip with Siri AI support, and more.
